title.narrative: Caring for Our Common Home: transformative connections towards climate, economic and social justice

description.narrative:
Brazil's Constitution guarantees the right to health and social protection. However the institutional and financial framework, coverage and access is inadequate. As a result, many of the poorest groups, particularly urban and rural periphery communities, lack access. Post-Pandemic, these groups are affected by cost-of-living crisis, high rates of unemployment, hunger, and GBV, and increasingly the impacts of climate change and environmental degradation. Social protection safety nets including unemployment, maternity, disability and sickness benefits, and state pensions are crucial in providing protection and dignity in difficult time. Inequality in access to health, an ill in itself, also compounds other inequalities. Access to universal health care and social protection are cornerstones of resilience to shocks and stresses. For example, well functioning environmental health services can reduce risk of dengue and zika outbreaks, which are becoming more frequent due to climate change. Emergency payments can enable those displaced by flooding to survive and rebuild. However, such systems are often poorly prepared, under-resourced, inaccessible to those in most need and lacking in accountability to local communities.
This project will support strengthening of activists and networks working to improve access to, coverage of and responsiveness of health and social protection systems in a context of increasing impacts of climate change related and environmental degradation. This will be carried out through training and accompaniment of leaders and civil society networks to enable more effective participation and monitoring of public policy processes, at local, subnational and federal level including of municipal and state-level plans and budgets and national level climate adaptation policies. In order to guarantee future sustainability and quality in the project, Grito will invest in institutional strengthening and communications capacity.
